W

Tread/riser joinery corrected, and the correction found by the new CAD kernel layer (cad/, audits/V-kernel-spike.md). The exposed face of every plumb notch is its downhill side — solid stringer is uphill of it — so the riser board goes in front of the cut (y₁ → y₁+¾) with its bottom edge resting on the stringer's horizontal cut for the tread below; that tread starts where the riser ends and butts its face. Simple butt joint, riser behind the tread, nothing notched. Rev V's note described the opposite arrangement and draw_treads() drew a third one — the riser recessed into solid stringer, which would have needed ten pocket-cut riser pieces instead of five boards. Consequences: every tread and riser is a full 24 wide, tread boards stay 9⅛, and the nosing-to-nosing going is exactly 9.000 at all five steps. Framing lines are unchanged; the finished nosings sit ⅞ downhill of them, so the stair's finished projection is 72⅞ (framing 72) and the landing 27⅞ (framing 27). lnd_ply is 27⅞ deep, not 27 — ¾ past the framing line for the riser-6 board, then the same ⅛ nose the treads get; Rev V typed that nose into Drawing 4 as a literal instead of carrying it on the member. Stringers notched 1½ × 3½ over the kicker at their floor seat: they had been drawn passing straight through it (7.87 cu in each), which verify.py cannot see because its stringer bearing rule checks plan overlap only. They are 7.54 deep there, so 6.04 remains. The kicker's position (y 68½→72) is no longer ASSUMED; its floor anchorage is still open. lnd_blocking stays at y 25½→27 — its front face is exactly the backing for the riser-6 board, as its note always said. Kernel check after the change: zero solid interferences in the stair and landing, and every cut face in Drawing 4 within 0.0043 of the kernel section (the sheet's own coordinate rounding).
